description: Erection of a ground floor side extension and timber clad garden studio and screening. Installation of air conditioning unit at the rear.
application_type_full: Householder planning & demolition in a conservation area
decision_conditions: <p>The outbuilding shall only be used as ancillary residential by the occupiers of the host dwelling.&nbsp;</p><p>REASON: To protect residential amenity&nbsp;</p>

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-1f6f4f8f-7fff-844a-24c9-bcef3a975fca"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management &amp; maintenance plan of at least one suitable sustainable drainage system (i.e. water butt with overflow, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof (substrate depth of 80-150mm excluding the vegetative mat), permeable paving etc.) shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume. Additionally, surface water runoff from the outbuilding should be drained sustainably and at source i.e. infiltration if it is not currently connected to the drainage system.</span></span></p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-1f6f4f8f-7fff-844a-24c9-bcef3a975fca"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">REASON: To promote sustainable drainage</span></span></p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-1f6f4f8f-7fff-844a-24c9-bcef3a975fca"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"> </span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-e441fc7a-7fff-fdbf-e8f4-c384a3a36a41"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the work, the applicant shall submit, and have approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, a detailed layout, cross sections (scale 1:20), full specifications and a detailed management and maintenance plan of the sedum roof with a minimum substrate depth of 80mm, not including the vegetative mat. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied.</span></span></p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-e441fc7a-7fff-fdbf-e8f4-c384a3a36a41"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">REASON: To promote sustainable drainage</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-fdc1df03-7fff-8f07-8127-04202c4e7830"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Any plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant,in accordance with BS4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.</span></span></p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-fdc1df03-7fff-8f07-8127-04202c4e7830"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">REASON: To protect neighbouring amenity</span></span></p>

<p>Only the proposed 1 no. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries multi-split outdoor
air-conditioning condenser unit, model SCM125ZM-S / SCM125ZS-W, as specified within the
submitted documentation, shall be installed at the premises. No alternative external plant,
compressors, or additional condenser machinery shall be installed without the express prior
written approval of the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>REASON: To protect neighbour amenity</p>

<div style="direction: ltr;">The outbuilding's foundation and sub-structure within the Root Protection Area (RPA) of the retained trees shall be implemented in strict accordance with the following requirements:</div><ul style="direction: ltr;"><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Foundation Type: The foundation for the outbuilding shall be constructed with hand tools only, using screw piles. No excavation, traditional strip foundations, continuous beams, or trenching shall be used within the RPAs of retained trees</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Gaseous Exchange: The finished sub-structure shall be a suspended ground floor/slab creating a ventilated air space between the underside of the structure and the existing soil surface to ensure:</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Gaseous Exchange: Free exchange of air and gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) between the soil and the atmosphere to maintain a healthy rooting environment.</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Soil Hydrology: The design should encourage the natural movement and infiltration of rainfall into the soil beneath the structure.</li></ul><div style="direction: ltr;">REASON: To safeguard the long-term health, stability, and viability of the retained tree(s)&nbsp;</div>

<p>All new underground utility apparatus, including drainage, shall be routed and installed outside the Root Protection Area(s) (RPAs) shown on the approved drawings. Should it not be feasible to route new underground utility apparatus outside the RPAs of retained trees, trenchless insertion methods (as detailed in BS 5837:2012, Table 3) shall be employed for their installation within the RPAs, with entry and retrieval pits sited outside the RPAs. No other new underground utilities shall be installed within the RPAs of retained trees without prior written consent from the Local Planning Authority (LPA). Any such works, if permitted, shall be carried out in strict accordance with the principles of BS 5837:2012 "Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations" and the National Joint Utilities Group Guidelines for the planning, installation and maintenance of utility apparatus in proximity to trees, Volume 4, Issue 2 (2007) (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this standard).<br><br>REASON: To safeguard existing tree(s) in the interests of visual amenity and long-term tree health.</p>

<div style="direction: ltr;">A new tree shall be planted in the rear garden of 62 Lordship Park, in the location illustratively shown on the approved document "(PL)010_3 SITE PLAN - PROPOSED (1).pdf" (Drawing No. 62LP-(PL)010-P03, dated 03.10.26). The tree planting must strictly comply with the following requirements: &nbsp;&nbsp;</div><ul style="direction: ltr;"><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Timing: The planting shall be completed during the first available bare-root planting season (October to March) following the removal of the existing tree.&nbsp;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Species: The species shall be mulberry (Morus nigra) unless the Local Planning Authority first agrees otherwise.&nbsp;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Size: The tree shall be planted as a minimum 'Light Standard' nursery stock (6-8cm stem girth measured at 1m above ground level).</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Standards: All planting, soil preparation, and staking shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard BS 8545:2014 (Trees: from nursery to independence in the landscape).</li><li style="margin-left: 15px; direction: ltr;">Retention and Replacement: If, within a period of five years from the date of planting, the tree dies, is removed, uprooted, or becomes seriously damaged or diseased, it shall be replaced in the next available planting season with another tree of the same species and size as that originally planted.</li></ul><div style="direction: ltr;">REASON: To mitigate the loss of the existing tree, to protect and enhance the visual amenity of the area.</div>
